To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment: product scope clarifications + operational priority (action lanes)

Team —

Orchid Health just shared a high-level ask: they want a Private (VPC) deployment with on-prem data egress restrictions and a 24/7 99.9% SLA. Their PMs (Ellen/Devon cc'd) want a feasibility snapshot we can use for their procurement committee by next Tues (5/27). I reviewed their runbook draft and attached our quick capacity estimates (see attached).

Open questions I need us to triage internally so we can give a crisp yes/no + list of non‑standard asks to their procurement:

- Product: which features are gated in Private deploy now (tool-calls, streaming, function calling)? any known product capabilities that require hosted control plane?
- Runtime/Arch: minimal footprint for their 2-model serving scenario (1x Llama-variant + 1x reranker), expected GPU types, and likely network topology constraints for air‑gapped subnets.
- Ops/Support: what oncall/responder mix do we need for a 99.9% SLA with private control plane (SRE vs Solutions)?
- Security/Compliance: quick callouts on evidence we can provide (audit logs, KMS integration, SOC surface).

Please reply with marked action lanes (Product / Runtime / Ops / Security) and one-sentence impact notes. I want a consolidated list by end-of-day Friday so I can send a short summary to Orchid.

Attachments: orchid_prod-runbook-draft.pdf, priv-deploy-capacity-scenarios.xlsx

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment: product scope clarifications + operational priority (action lanes)

Karthik —

Product lane: quick bullets —
- Feature availability: streaming and function/tool calling are available in Private but require feature-flagging on the private control plane; there are documented telemetry differences (we do not stream control-plane events to hosted analytics).
- Data flow: prefix/KV caching can be enabled but cache persistence across restarts is not supported in the current private runtime (we should call this out).
- Workarounds: if Orchid needs hosted telemetry for quality monitoring, we can provide a proxy collector but it is a non-standard integration.

Impact: core generation + reranking features supported; extra effort for telemetry and durable cache.

Quick ask: Product to confirm whether the customer will accept MEP (metrics export proxy) vs hosted telemetry.

—Marissa
Sr. PM, Product
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2025-05-18T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: product scope clarifications + operational priority (action lanes)

Arch/Runtime lane: short answers and capacity sketch —
- Minimal footprint: for 2-model serving (gen + reranker), recommend 2x A100-40GB (or equivalent A10G if cost-constrained) with dedicated KV cache memory per model; if Orchid requires sustained concurrent requests (>400 RPS) we should propose sharded pools.
- Network: private control plane + customer-managed VPC peering is doable; for air‑gapped subnets we will package an on‑prem runtime bundle but we need a temporary bootstrap link for versioning and agent health checks (can be done via scheduled outbound only egress to our update service).
- Non-standard: air‑gapped full isolation (no outbound) will require manual image delivery + an extended support runbook. Estimate +2 SRE weeks to establish image pipeline and +1 eng week for ops automation.

Attachments: (I updated the capacity spreadsheet with two scenarios)

—Jonas
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Ops/Support lane: notes —
- SLA staffing: to meet 99.9% with private control plane we need a rotated oncall that includes 1 dedicated Solutions Engineer (tier 2) and SRE support during business hours, plus an escalation path to infra on-call for infra-level incidents. Rough estimate: 0.4 FTE Solutions (per pilot), 0.2 FTE SRE sustained; higher during pilot runway.
- Runbook: I can produce a 2-page runbook for customer-facing incident triage if we agree on the escalation windows.
- Pricing impact: premium support add-on recommended — call S&M to price for Orchid.

Action: assign Solutions lead (Grace?) for runbook coauthoring and handoff to Sales for SOW line items.

—Stephanie

Thanks all — consolidation and next steps for Orchid:

1) Marissa: confirm telemetry choice (MEP proxy vs hosted telemetry) by EOD Fri 5/23. If MEP, Solutions will draft integration checklist; if hosted, note the analytics limitations in the SOW.
2) Jonas: finalize capacity scenarios (A100 vs A10G) and delivery options for air‑gapped image pipeline; drop final numbers in the shared spreadsheet by 5/23.
3) Stephanie & Grace: coauthor 2-page customer runbook + pilot checklist; initial draft to Orchid by 5/26.
4) Sales/Solutions: prepare SOW line items for premium support and image-delivery work (Karthik will loop in Sales after we have cost estimates).

Karthik will compile a 1-page feasibility memo for Orchid (target: Monday 5/26 morning internal send, then to customer after any redlines). If any lane cannot meet the ask, flag it immediately.

Ellen/Devon — thanks for the context. We'll push the feasibility memo to you next week. Any firm constraints on outbound bootstrap traffic (IP whitelist windows) would be helpful now.
